evidence: Quote found verbatim: design/manuscript/chapter-10/chapter-10.md L169 'the total expert residency that must be sharded, and the all-to-all routing it forces'. The pronoun 'it' refers to the sharding named in the same list, so 'forces' is already conditional on expert sharding — under EP dispatch, all-to-all is indeed forced (L19: EP 'routes each token to the GPU holding its experts — an all-to-all exchange per token'). The alternatives the finding cites (replicated experts, expert caching) avoid all-to-all only by avoiding the sharding the sentence names; the sentence does not claim all MoE serving requires all-to-all. The finding's 'universal MoE requirement' reading is not supported by the antecedent.

Both fragments found in chapter-10.md L169: 'the total expert residency that must be sharded' and 'since the full expert set occupies HBM even when only a fraction is routed per token'. The latter is asserted unconditionally as the reason the memory-bound EP decision is made against total parameters; no condition (deployment requires all experts resident) and no alternative (expert offloading/caching) appears anywhere in the bullet. Large-MoE serving can offload or cache experts, so all-experts-HBM-resident is a deployment assumption presented as a universal property.
fix_instruction: chapter-10.md L169: qualify the residency clause, e.g. '...is made against total parameters when the deployment keeps the full expert set resident in HBM (expert offloading/caching changes this calculus), even when only a fraction is routed per token.'

evidence: Both fragments found in chapter-10.md L175: 'Within each node, the MoE active weights are small ... checked against the node's 640 GB HBM'. The full line reads: 'the MoE active weights are small (state the split explicitly: ~40B active of the 400B total [ASSUMPTION], checked against the node's 640 GB HBM), so the team uses EP to shard the total expert set (EP shards total residency, not the active count)'. The HBM residency check is performed on active bytes (40B x 2 = 80 GB vs 640 GB) while the text itself states the correct constraint is total-sharded residency; total resident bytes per node after EP sharding (800 GB total / N nodes) are never computed against 640 GB anywhere in the mini-case.
fix_instruction: chapter-10.md L175: compute total resident bytes per node after EP sharding (total expert bytes / number of EP nodes, plus TP shards) and check THAT against 640 GB; use active parameters only for the compute/FLOP statement, not the HBM residency check.

evidence: Quote found verbatim: chapter-11.md L60 'the mechanism makes the GPU the steady bottleneck instead of the scheduler. [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]'. The same paragraph's own caveat conflicts with it: L60 'idle can still occur from insufficient arrivals, KV capacity, prefill, or scheduling policy' — if scheduling policy can still cause idle, the scheduler can still bind, which 'instead of the scheduler' denies. fix_instruction: chapter-11.md L60: replace 'the mechanism makes the GPU the steady bottleneck instead of the scheduler' with 'the mechanism shifts the bottleneck from batch-boundary idle time toward GPU resources when arrivals and KV capacity permit — scheduler policy, KV capacity and arrival rate can still bind'.

evidence: Quote found verbatim: design/manuscript/chapter-14/chapter-14.md L34 'C ≈ 17.5 (the 436 GB canonical KV budget ÷ 24.9 GB per 9,500-token whole-context request)'. Grep of chapter-14.md for FP16/FP8/2.62/1.31 returns no KV-precision statement anywhere in the chapter. Arithmetic verified both ways: 9,500 x 2.62 MB = 24.89 GB -> 436/24.89 = 17.52 (FP16); 9,500 x 1.31 MB = 12.45 GB -> 436/12.45 = 35.03 (8-bit). The quotient silently selects FP16 (confirmed as canonical elsewhere: chapter-15.md L84 '≈2.62 MB/token × 9,500' = 24.9 GB; chapter-17.md L284 '17.5 sequences on FP16 at T=0'), but the chunk never labels the precision, so the reader cannot reproduce 24.9 GB from tokens without guessing, and the 8-bit reading of the same quotient gives C ≈ 35.
fix_instruction: chapter-14.md L34: state the precision in the quotient, e.g. 'C ≈ 17.5 FP16-KV request-equivalents (436 GB FP16 KV budget ÷ 24.9 GB per 9,500-token request; 9,500 × 2.62 MB ≈ 24.9 GB)' — and if any 8-bit row is intended, recompute C ≈ 35 and update the 17-slot, 1.98 req/s, 2.03 req/s and ~3% gap figures consistently.

Quote found verbatim: chapter-14.md L130 'Bigger batch sizes raise tokens/s but push TTFT over the deadline, zeroing goodput (Ch6, Ch11).' The bullet asserts an unconditional zeroing; the chapter's own goodput definition makes it continuous: chapter-14.md L51 '| SLO-goodput | tokens/s meeting the SLO (Ch 6), not raw throughput |'. If only the tail of TTFT crosses the deadline, some requests still meet the SLO and goodput is positive but lower; it reaches zero only when no request in the window complies. The claim strength exceeds the mechanism as written.
fix_instruction: chapter-14.md L130: replace 'zeroing goodput' with 'and can reduce goodput — to zero only if no request in the measurement window meets the SLO' (or 'pushing TTFT over the deadline for the affected requests and cutting SLO-compliant goodput').

evidence: Quote found verbatim: chapter-14.md L15 'Two models with identical MMLU can differ wildly in TTFT under the same batching, because serving depends on tokenizer, context length, KV layout, and scheduler — none of which a leaderboard scores.' The sentence's function is to contrast leaderboard-scored factors with serving factors; 'depends on A, B, C, D' is an illustrative list, not an asserted exhaustive one, and the finding's own evidence hedges ('could let a reader infer'). Model size/architecture/hardware are indeed first-order for TTFT, but the sentence does not state they are irrelevant, and the qualifier 'under the same batching' scopes the comparison. A breadth/completeness preference, not a stated error.

The later paragraph does not contradict it — it hooks back to that exact phrase: L77 'One subtlety about "matching its own distribution": the target does *not* simply accept the draft tokens that happen to agree ... the acceptance criterion must be the correction procedure, not mere token equality', and it notes 'For greedy/argmax decoding the agreement test is exact'.
